title: ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Review
gist: ServeTheHome's hardware overview of ASUS's sub-$2,000 Turbo Radeon AI Pro R9700, AMD's 32GB Navi 48/RDNA 4 workstation AI card positioned as a cheaper alternative to NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell. It gains FP8 compute (382.7 dense TFLOPS) but regresses in VRAM versus the 48GB W7900, and is built as a 300W dual-slot blower for four-card workstations. The text covers hardware only; the performance section is not included.

themes.theme: AMD rebrands workstation GPUs for AI

insights.claim: AMD has repositioned its professional Radeon Pro workstation GPU line as the Radeon AI Pro lineup, making it the backbone of its add-in card AI accelerator efforts.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Signals AMD pushing local/workstation AI inference as a distinct product segment beyond datacenter Instinct parts.
insights.quote: The Radeon Pro lineup, once the backbone of AMD’s workstation graphics efforts, has become the Radeon AI Pro lineup
insights.locator: Within the AMD ecosystem, the company

insights.claim: The 32GB AMD Radeon AI Pro R9700 is positioned by AMD and partners as a more budget-friendly alternative to NVIDIA's RTX PRO Blackwell workstation cards, with ASUS's version selling for under $2,000.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: AMD is competing on price/VRAM per dollar against NVIDIA in workstation AI; watch for share shifts in local inference hardware.

insights.claim: Although datacenter servers dominate AI inference attention, workstation video cards remain an important AI market segment where the AI revolution originated.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Workstation/local AI GPU demand is a secondary but durable revenue stream for GPU vendors and board partners.
insights.locator: While much of the attention in the market

insights.claim: AMD is not selling its own reference-design Radeon AI Pro R9700 workstation cards this generation, leaving sales to board partners such as ASUS, which is unusual for workstation GPUs.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Shifts workstation GPU margin and channel to board partners like ASUS.
insights.locator: As AMD is not selling their own reference design

insights.claim: AMD keeps Radeon AI Pro partners on a short leash, so all partner R9700 cards are similar dual-slot blower designs engineered to allow up to four cards in one workstation.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Multi-GPU density is the core selling point for local AI workloads; partner differentiation is limited.
insights.quote: AMD has been keeping their Radeon Pro partners on a rather short leash with card designs.

insights.claim: The Radeon AI Pro R9700 uses AMD's Navi 48 RDNA 4 GPU with 64 CUs, 4096 shading units and 128 AI accelerator cores, delivering 382.7 TFLOPS of dense FP8 matrix throughput (double with sparsity) and 47.8 TFLOPS FP32 at a 2.92GHz boost clock.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Benchmark reference point for comparing AMD workstation AI compute against NVIDIA RTX PRO parts.
insights.locator: Under the hood, the card is powered

insights.claim: RDNA 4 adds FP8 support, which raises compute throughput and aligns AMD hardware with the industry trend toward lower-precision weights that fit more parameters in a given memory capacity.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Closes a feature gap with NVIDIA for low-precision inference, improving AMD's software/model compatibility story.
insights.locator: One of the key improvements in this generation

insights.claim: Navi 48 is a mid-to-high-end die at 357mm2 and 53.9B transistors; AMD produced no true high-end GPU in the RDNA 4 generation.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: AMD skipped the top-end consumer/pro tier this generation, ceding the high end to NVIDIA.

insights.claim: The R9700 carries 32GB of GDDR6 at 20Gbps on a 256-bit bus (640GB/s) in a clamshell configuration, with soft ECC available only under Linux and only when manually enabled.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Bandwidth of 640GB/s constrains LLM token throughput versus HBM or GDDR7-based competitors.
insights.locator: On that note, as is traditional

insights.claim: Memory capacity is AMD's key differentiator between consumer and professional cards, with 32GB available only on Radeon AI Pro cards.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: VRAM segmentation is how AMD protects pro-card pricing; capacity per dollar drives local-AI purchasing.
insights.quote: Above all else, memory support is a key differentiator between AMD’s consumer and professional cards

insights.claim: Because AMD lacked a high-end RDNA 4 die, the 32GB R9700 has less VRAM than the previous-generation 48GB Radeon Pro W7900, a step back in capacity that AMD aims to offset with higher compute throughput.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Buyers running large models may prefer prior-gen 48GB cards or NVIDIA options; capacity regression is a weakness for AI workloads.
insights.quote: the R9700 actually has less VRAM than the previous-generation 48GB Radeon Pro W7900
insights.locator: AMD did not produce a true high-end GPU

insights.claim: The smaller Navi 48 chip keeps the R9700's total board power at 300W, making four cards in one system feasible without excessive power, though near the limit of a single power supply.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Enables 128GB-VRAM four-GPU workstations on standard PSUs, a practical edge for local inference rigs.
insights.locator: One advantage of being a smaller chip

insights.claim: ASUS's Turbo Radeon AI Pro R9700 uses an open-backed dual-ball-bearing blower and places its 600W-rated 12V-2x6 power connector at the rear of the card to ease multi-card installation.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Workstation-specific mechanical design choices matter for dense multi-GPU builds.
insights.locator: Being that this is a workstation card

insights.claim: The ASUS Turbo R9700 provides three DisplayPort 2.1a outputs and one HDMI 2.1b output, the maximum four displays Navi 48 can drive, supporting up to 12K resolution with DSC.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Retains full graphics/visualization use alongside AI, broadening the addressable workstation buyer.
